environment.name: STREAMSPLAYER_DATA_DIRECTORY
environment.description: A fully qualified folder. The process then keeps its state there and is an instance of its own (its lock and pipe names carry a profile hash), so commands reach only the copy that runs with the same value.

commands.name: commands
commands.summary: Print the list of commands this product accepts.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the manifest itself as JSON.

exitCodes.meaning: printed

examples.expect: the manifest as an object; exit 0, no window opens and no running copy is needed

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Print the product name, its version and the version of its command set.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the response line itself instead of a sentence.

exitCodes.meaning: printed

commands.name: status
commands.summary: Say whether StreamsPlayer is running and ready to take commands.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the response line itself.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

returns.name: acceptsRestrictedCommands
returns.description: whether the setting that lets other programs ask for more than the safe commands is on

returns.name: activeSessions
returns.description: how many streams play now (a count only)

returns.name: profile
returns.description: default, or relocated when STREAMSPLAYER_DATA_DIRECTORY is in force

exitCodes.meaning: running and ready
not running, or busy (a dialog is open or the app is closing)

examples.expect: the response object, then 0 while the app runs and is ready, 11 otherwise

commands.name: show
commands.summary: Bring the main window forward; started with no arguments the app opens (or comes forward) and plays nothing.

exitCodes.meaning: the window is forward
busy (a dialog is open or the app is closing)

commands.name: quit
commands.summary: Close the running StreamsPlayer cleanly; with none running there is nothing to do.

exitCodes.meaning: closed, or was not running
the close has not finished within the bound; the app may still be closing
busy (a dialog is open)

examples.expect: exit 0 (errorlevel 0) once the app has closed, or at once when it was not running

commands.name: play
commands.summary: Play a saved channel, a stream address or a StreamsPlayer broadcast resource file.

args.name: id
args.description: A saved channel's id. Exactly one target is required: --id (optionally with --url or --url-file), --url, --url-file, or --file.

args.name: url
args.description: A stream address (http, https or rtsp). With --id it is the fallback that finds the channel again after a catalog refresh replaced its row. May carry a credential; never logged or returned.

args.name: url-file
args.description: A file whose one UTF-8 line is the stream address, for an address that carries a credential and must stay out of the command line and the shell history. Taken in place of --url; a relative path is taken from the caller's working folder.

args.name: file
args.description: A .spres broadcast resource document: it is imported, then played.

args.name: background
args.description: Do not bring the window forward.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the response line itself.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

exitCodes.meaning: playing: the first sound or picture arrived, or the stream already played
the stream did not open (reason stream-failed)
no sound or picture within the bound; the app may still be trying
no target, two targets, an address that is not http, https or rtsp, an empty --url-file, or an unreadable .spres
busy, --id is not in the catalog and no --url was given, or the file of --url-file does not exist (reason target-missing)
the broadcast needs a link password that is not stored on this PC (reason needs-person); the command never asks for it
the file of --url-file cannot be read (reason io-error)
the stream's host could not be reached

examples.expect: exit 0 once the radio is audible
0 once the stream of the address on the first line of the file plays; the address never appears on the command line or in the log

commands.name: playback stop
commands.summary: Stop the playing stream (all of them with --all); nothing playing is already the goal.

args.name: id
args.description: The channel to stop. Required (or --all) when more than one stream plays.

args.name: all
args.description: Stop every playing stream.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

exitCodes.meaning: stopped, or nothing was playing
several streams play and neither --id nor --all was given, or both were
busy (a modal dialog is open)

commands.name: playback pause
commands.summary: Pause the playing radio (the audio session). Video windows have no pause.

exitCodes.meaning: paused, or already paused
not running, busy, or no radio is playing
playing again, or was not paused
the stream did not open again
no sound within the bound
not running, busy, or there is no radio session to resume
the stream's host could not be reached

examples.expect: exit 0 once the radio is audible

commands.name: playback status
commands.summary: List what plays now: kind, channel, title, state and whether it is being recorded.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the response line itself.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

returns.name: sessions
returns.description: one object per open stream: kind (audio or video), channelId, title, state (playing, paused, buffering, failed), recording (bool). The stream address is never included.

exitCodes.meaning: listed (an empty list when nothing plays)
the list is over the 64 KiB bound of an answer (reason response-too-large)
not running, or busy
the setting of rule 13 is off

examples.expect: one object per open stream while the setting is on

commands.name: volume set
commands.summary: Set the volume of the radio or of the video players, and mute or unmute video.

args.name: target
args.description: Which volume: the radio's or the video players'.

args.name: muted
args.description: Mute or unmute; accepted for video only.

exitCodes.meaning: set
level outside 0-100, or --muted with the audio target
not running, or busy

commands.name: record start
commands.summary: Start recording a playing stream into a folder the caller names; nothing is ever written anywhere else.

args.name: out
args.description: The folder the recording is written into: an existing folder, which this command never creates. A relative path is taken from the caller's working folder. The file name inside it is the product's own (CAPTURE-OUTPUT: kind, prefix, name) and an existing file is never replaced.

args.name: id
args.description: The playing channel to record; optional when exactly one stream is open.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

returns.name: folder
returns.description: the folder the recording is written into, as the caller named it, in full

returns.name: file
returns.description: the file being written, inside the folder; given for a radio recording only - a video file is named when it ends, see record stop

exitCodes.meaning: recording: the first recorded data was seen (a second start on the same stream into the same folder answers the same recording)
the stream cannot be recorded (reason not-recordable: a StreamsPlayer broadcast, a format a byte copy cannot record) or the recording could not start (error, stream-failed)
no recorded data was seen within the bound; the recording may still be starting - run the command again, or record stop
no --out, a doubled --out or --id, several streams open and no --id, or --out is a file and not a folder

not running, busy, no stream is open or the named one is not, the radio is paused or the stream failed, the stream is already recorded into another folder, or the folder of --out does not exist (reason target-missing)
the setting of rule 13 is off
no space for the recording (reason no-space)
the folder of --out cannot be written (reason io-error)

examples.expect: 0 while a stream plays and the setting is on

commands.name: record stop
commands.summary: Finish the recording and report the file, its size and its length.

args.name: id
args.description: The channel being recorded; optional when exactly one recording runs.

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

returns.name: file
returns.description: the finished file in the folder of record start; the first one when parts is above 1

returns.name: bytes
returns.description: its size in bytes, all parts together

returns.name: seconds
returns.description: the recorded length, all parts together

returns.name: parts
returns.description: how many files the recording is in: more than 1 only when the stream dropped and was opened again while recording

exitCodes.meaning: the file is finished
the recording ended with nothing saved
finishing has not ended within the bound; the file may still be completing
a doubled --id, or several recordings run and no --id
not running, busy, nothing is being recorded or the named stream is not, or the recording is already being finished
the setting of rule 13 is off
no space to finish the recording (reason no-space)
the file could not be written or moved into the folder (reason io-error)

examples.line: StreamsPlayerCli.exe record stop --result C:\temp\rec.json; Get-Content C:\temp\rec.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
examples.expect: an object with file, bytes, seconds and parts

commands.name: channel add
commands.summary: Add a stream address to the user's own list (a Manual channel that a catalog refresh never touches).

args.name: url
args.description: A stream address (http, https or rtsp). May carry a credential; never logged or returned. Exactly one of --url and --url-file is required.

args.name: url-file
args.description: A file whose one UTF-8 line is the stream address, for an address that carries a credential and must stay out of the command line and the shell history. A relative path is taken from the caller's working folder.

args.name: title
args.description: The channel's title; the address's host when absent.

args.name: collection
args.description: An existing collection to put the channel in (never created by this command).

args.name: result
args.description: Where to write the response data as JSON.

returns.name: channelId
returns.description: the new channel's id, or the existing one

returns.name: created
returns.description: false when the address was already in the list

exitCodes.meaning: added, or already there
no address, both --url and --url-file, an empty --url-file, an address that is not http, https or rtsp, or a repeated option
busy (a catalog refresh or a dialog is open), --collection names no collection, or the file of --url-file does not exist (reason target-missing)
the catalog could not be saved, or the file of --url-file cannot be read (reason io-error)

examples.expect: exit 0; the channel is in My streams
